stem: Using the Pauling electronegativities H = 2.1, C = 2.5, N = 3.0, O = 3.5 and F = 4.0, which order gives decreasing bond polarity?

verdicts.working: Bond polarity follows the electronegativity difference: H–F = 1.9, O–H = 1.4, N–H = 0.9, C–H = 0.4.

working:
$\Delta\chi(\text{H–F})=1.9$; $\Delta\chi(\text{O–H})=1.4$; $\Delta\chi(\text{N–H})=0.9$; $\Delta\chi(\text{C–H})=0.4$.\
Bond polarity increases with electronegativity difference.

Independent check: Bond polarity follows the electronegativity difference: H–F = 1.9, O–H = 1.4, N–H = 0.9, C–H = 0.4.
solution:
Bond polarity increases with the electronegativity difference, $\Delta\chi=|\chi_A-\chi_B|$.
$$\Delta\chi(\text{H–F})=1.9>\Delta\chi(\text{O–H})=1.4>\Delta\chi(\text{N–H})=0.9>\Delta\chi(\text{C–H})=0.4$$
Hence the decreasing order is $\text{H–F} > \text{O–H} > \text{N–H} > \text{C–H}$.
